The Prize Competition Act, 1955, the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 and the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 were enacted under Article 252 on resolutions of two or more States. The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is not an Article 252 law; it was enacted to implement an international (Stockholm) commitment, i.e. under Article 253.

A GST Council decision needs three-fourths of the weighted votes. The Centre holds only one-third and all States together only two-thirds, so neither side can reach three-fourths alone; options A-C misstate the voting rules.
Special category States had the first charge on Central Plan assistance and received it on the favourable terms of 90 percent grant and 10 percent loan.

Article 356(5) allows President's Rule to continue beyond one year only if a National Emergency is in operation and the Election Commission certifies that elections cannot be held. Deferring State polls under ONOE could prolong President's Rule and clash with this limit.

The 1973 spell of President's Rule in Andhra Pradesh (following the Jai Andhra agitation) ended after the Six-Point Formula, which was validated by the 32nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1973 inserting Article 371D.
